newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end slightly higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end slightly higher in thin trade.

text.p: Thai stocks ended slightly higher on Tuesday as late buying nudged the index into positive territory after a dull afternoon session, analysts said.
The SET Index gained 2.21 points, or 0.26 percent, to 842.63. The SET 50 ended up 0.27 points at 63.35. Volumes were a meagre 2.29 billion baht.
"It was very boring. There was some interest but it was pretty selective ... It's too late to sell and too early to buy," said Rob Collins, head of research at Asia Equity.

There was some limited foreign buying of telecommunications stocks, but the market was set for a quiet period ahead of any concrete evidence of a recovery and more corporate earnings results, Collins said.

"Some people are switching into telecommunications as a classic defensive play. Most foreigners seem quite bullish on the Thai market and give it a maximum downside of 10 percent, but are not yet prepared to put their money there," he said.
The communications sector did attract limited interest and gained 0.70 percent, otherwise there was mostly short term retail speculation in bank and finance counters, traders said.
Shares of mobile phone network provider Advanced Info Services, the main focus of recent buying of mobile phone stocks, topped the active list and extended its recent run by gaining four to 272.
Mobile phone firm International Engineering closed up 2.25 baht to 52, and Thai Farmers Bank was up two baht to 128.
Decliners edged out advancers 145 to 114, 112 issues closed unchanged.
